scope: A payout was recorded, queued and then blocked because no payment authority existed. Adds the live Remesso adapter and, more importantly, an account of what a payment authority can actually deliver: one token approval is shared by every policy the same wallet grants, so per-campaign budgets say nothing about solvency and two live briefs could each believe they were funded. Payout gas is read from each transaction’s own receipt and reported in the currency it was paid in, which closes one of the economics target’s holes without making it measurable. Each approval is re-read on a timer that reschedules itself, and a read that failed is kept strictly apart from an approval that is genuinely short. What that read finds is raised once as a notice, resolved when it stops, and delivered as a signed POST that records whether anyone was told

accounting.approvalIdentity: chain, token and payer: the tuple that identifies the approval on chain, not the workspace, policy or authority that references it
accounting.ceiling: CHECK (committed_units <= declared_units), so no application path can let two campaigns promise the same units
moves: commit reserves against every other brief
release returns only what no payable still needs
accounting.replayable: every move is an appended immutable entry; the row replays from them, so closing a brief twice releases nothing the second time
accounting.secondHandleOnOneWallet: describes the same approval rather than adding to it
accounting.declarationMonotonic: a declaration can only rise; a shrunken approval is a shortfall found by reading, not a record to edit
accounting.solvencyTest: min(allowance, balance) >= committed; an allowance nobody can fund pays nothing

adapter.name: remesso
adapter.funding: policy, named by the payable’s own authority; a payable with no authority is refused rather than defaulted
adapter.maxDebit: the recipient amount exactly, so a protocol fee appearing later refuses the send
adapter.confirmedMeansInclusion: a send the SDK reports as confirmed is mapped to included, never to finality
adapter.confirmUses: reconcile, which continues a started payment and never starts a new one
adapter.unknownKey: a key the provider has no record of returns unknown, the only state in which the key may be sent again
adapter.journals: remesso-sdk/postgres in Trialoom’s own database through a pg bridge over its structural postgres.js interface; queries on one connection are chained because the signer’s session advisory lock lives on it
adapter.keySource: TRIALOOM_REMESSO_AGENT_KEY; absent in this build, so the unconfigured adapter still blocks every payout

checks.fork: 19 checks against deployed contract code on a disposable Anvil fork of Celo, exit 0
covered: two briefs cannot both promise one shared approval; the refusal leaves the first published and the second a draft, and what fits is still publishable to the last base unit
a second authority on the same wallet resolves to one approval row and states the same amount rather than doubling it, while a different wallet has its own room
a declaration rises and is never edited downwards; the entries explain the number and the row replays from them
a forced UPDATE past the declared remainder is refused by the table check
publication must name an authority once one exists, and the authority is fixed at first publication
a finalized payout spends the approval instead of freeing it, and the declared remainder falls with it
closing a brief returns its remainder but keeps everything still owed on a payable reserved
a revoked authority blocks the payout with a named reason, pauses the brief, keeps the debt exactly as accepted, and funds nothing new

verification refuses with no provider configured; a reading below the commitments marks the approval short and cancels nothing; an inactive policy is short whatever the numbers say; observations are immutable

on a Celo fork with a real policy: the reader reads the live approval and balance, the worker settles a real payable from included to finality, exactly the owed amount reaches the payee in one signed transaction, the approval records the spend, a re-read of the chain agrees, the same key again moves nothing, and a policy revoked on chain reads as short

over real HTTP: an owner registers an authority, sees one shared approval across two handles on the same wallet, is refused a reading with no provider configured, and revokes it with what that does and does not do stated
what a payout cost to send is recorded once per transaction, however many times the adapter reports the same receipt, and the builder’s ledger and the amount owed are untouched by it
a gas reading is immutable and undeletable, and a cost that is not gas used times the price paid is refused by the table
gas paid in the settlement token is comparable with revenue, gas paid in CELO is not, and the two are never summed into one number
the economics target stops reporting payout gas as missing, names the recorded cost in the currency it was paid in, and still prints no margin
on the fork: the agent’s own CELO balance fell by exactly the recorded gas while the payee’s USDC rose by exactly the amount owed
registering an authority starts a recurring read that records the same evidence a person’s read would leave, with no actor behind it, and puts itself back on the queue
a read that failed is recorded as unread without touching the previous reading or the approval’s state, does not spend the attempts that would kill the job, and is cleared by a later success
a policy the chain says is inactive stops new claims and keeps the accepted obligation exactly as accepted, while a shortfall on an active policy pauses nothing
revoking an authority ends its recurring read rather than leaving it spinning, and no further observation arrives
the queue names an approval nobody has read, one whose reading has gone stale, and one that is short, and leaves a fresh covering reading alone
on the fork, the worker’s own dispatch drove the recurring read against the real chain through verified, then inactive after the policy was revoked on chain, then revoked
a shortfall is raised once however often it is re-read, resolved when the approval covers its commitments, and raised again if it returns
a read nobody could complete is raised as its own condition and closed by a later successful read; revoking the authority closes everything it raised
a workspace with nowhere to be told records that the notice reached nobody and queues nothing; registering a destination requeues what is already open
a destination that refuses leaves the notice undelivered with its attempt recorded, and the retry does not spend the attempts that would retire the job
a condition that cleared before delivery is suppressed rather than sent
one real signed POST was verified by a loopback receiver that checked the signature itself; the same body under a different timestamp or a different key does not verify
a destination in private space and a second live destination are both refused
the table refuses a notice carrying a credential at three different depths

forkBoundaries: every transaction goes to loopback on a disposable Anvil fork the script starts and stops; the upstream Celo node is only read
the signing keys are the public Anvil fixture accounts, and the script refuses to run with TRIALOOM_REMESSO_AGENT_KEY set
Anvil reports finalized sixty-four blocks behind latest, so the check mines past that distance; real finality timing is unmeasured
no mainnet transaction, no funded wallet, and no evidence of production behaviour or event eligibility
limits: no mainnet transaction and no funded wallet, so nothing here establishes production behaviour or real finality timing
the agent key comes from the environment, with no rotation and no hardware signer; a compromised process can spend up to the policy caps
one signer, serialized by the SDK coordinator, so payout throughput is one transaction at a time per agent address
recoverPending is not wired to a schedule; recovery happens when the outbox retries a payable
no webhook or indexer: payment state is pulled when a job runs rather than pushed on inclusion
the platform fee recipient and the resource recipient are still unconfigured, so those payables block for a missing recipient rather than a missing authority
an authority is fixed at a brief’s first publication, so moving a live brief to another wallet needs the brief closed
remesso-sdk 0.3.1 exists and is not adopted
a CELO gas cost cannot be set against USDC revenue without a price feed, which does not exist here, so the economics target reports the two separately and prints no margin
only payout gas is recorded: a resource purchase is also sent by a platform wallet and also costs gas, but no live resource adapter exists to read a receipt from
a receipt that cannot be read is not recorded and nothing retries it, because the job completes at finality
the re-read interval is fixed in code rather than per workspace: six hours suits a pilot, and a busy workspace on a shared wallet would want minutes

a notice goes to a URL rather than to a person: there is still no email and no platform-reviewer channel, and a workspace that registers no destination is back to reading the queue, with the difference that the platform records that nobody was told
review escalation could use this channel and does not yet; that belongs with PILOT-01
no reminders: an open notice is delivered once and then waits for the condition to clear, so a shortfall nobody acts on for a week is not raised again

a real HTTPS delivery from a registered row is untested, because registration refuses a loopback URL by design; the transport is tested against a loopback server and the orchestration against the database

gas.table: payout_gas, immutable, one row per transaction hash
gas.source: the transaction receipt (gasUsed, effectiveGasPrice) and the transaction itself (Celo feeCurrency), not an estimate
gas.idempotentPerTransaction: UNIQUE (transaction_hash), so an adapter may report the same receipt on every poll
gas.platformCostOnly: never enters the campaign ledger, the builder’s liability or the token approval; the approval funds the transfer, the agent’s own balance funds its gas
gas.currenciesNeverConverted: readings are grouped by the currency each was paid in, each stating whether it is the currency the fee is collected in; an unrecognised fee currency is recorded with no decimals rather than shifted by a guessed exponent
gas.economicsEffect: the target names a real cost instead of an absence and still refuses to print a margin: compute, verification, human review and refunds remain unrecorded
gas.measuredOnTheFork: the agent’s CELO balance fell by exactly the recorded cost while the payee’s USDC rose by exactly the amount owed

verification.schedule: enqueued on the same outbox in the transaction that registers the authority, so an approval cannot exist unchecked; each turn reschedules itself rather than depending on a cron, and revoking the authority ends the job
verification.failedReadIsNotAReading: the attempt is recorded before the call and the error afterwards; the previous reading and the state are untouched, and a later success clears it. An RPC outage must not be indistinguishable from insolvency
verification.failedReadIsAWait: the retry is sooner than the interval and does not spend the attempts that would kill the job, because a recurring read that dies after five bad answers stops checking exactly when checking matters

whatAReadingMayDo.policyInactive: stops new claims on every brief it funds, because it is the same fact a failed payout would report later, and erases nothing accepted
whatAReadingMayDo.approvalShort: reported and nothing else: a moving number the builder can top up, and pausing live work on it would turn a temporary balance into a stopped campaign
whatAReadingMayDo.readFailed: reported as unread; the previous reading stands

verification.workerCarriesTheLiveAdapter: fixed here: configuredPayments was reached only by the verification route, so nothing would have paid through the adapter in production. The worker builds the adapter and reader once and says which it has at startup

notices.raiseAndResolve: raised when a condition becomes true and resolved when it stops; one open notice per topic and subject enforced by a partial unique index rather than by application logic

whetherAnyoneWasTold.undeliverable: the workspace has nowhere to be told
whetherAnyoneWasTold.failed: the destination refused it, with every attempt kept
whetherAnyoneWasTold.suppressed: the condition resolved before delivery; stale news sends the builder looking for something that is not there

notices.retryIsAWait: a destination that is down is not a failing handler, so retrying does not spend the attempts that would retire the job
notices.destinationAdmission: the same rules as a test target: HTTPS, no credentials or query in the URL, and an address outside private space. One live destination per workspace, so the question has one answer
notices.signature: X-Trialoom-Timestamp plus X-Trialoom-Signature, sha256= followed by HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp.body; signing the timestamp as well as the body means a captured body cannot be replayed under a new one
notices.oneWay: redirects refused and nothing read from the response beyond its status: a receiver that could answer back would be a way into the platform
notices.secretAtRest: stored rather than digested, because the platform presents a signature rather than recognising one. Shown once, never returned, never selected by a read path, never travels in a notice
notices.nothingLeavesWithACredential: the body is composed from the platform’s own records, never from operator prose, and the detail column reuses event_payload_is_clean so a key or grant is refused at any depth by the table
